after.title: 1.6L Coolant-Loss and Cylinder-Head Fire Recalls
after.description: NHTSA campaign 12V551 covers certain 2013 Fusion 1.6L vehicles whose coolant-system leaks can overheat the engine and release flammable fluids. Campaign 17V209 covers certain 2013-2014 Fusion 1.6L vehicles in which driving with insufficient coolant can overheat and crack the cylinder head, allowing an oil leak and increasing fire risk.
after.solution: Check the VIN for every open Ford campaign. The 12V551 remedy includes a coolant-system leak inspection plus updated PCM and instrument-cluster overheat strategy. The 17V209 remedy installs a coolant-level sensor with supporting hardware and software. Ford dealers perform covered recall work free of charge; an overheated, smoking, or leaking engine should be shut down and inspected rather than driven.

after.description: Ford TSB 20-2100 applies to some 2014-2019 Fusion vehicles with the 1.5L EcoBoost built on or before 10-Jun-2019. Low coolant, white exhaust smoke, rough running, and specified misfire or overtemperature codes can result from coolant entering a cylinder.
after.solution: A technician should pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the cylinders under Ford service procedures. after.title: Program 13N03: Throttle-Body Motor-Contact Contamination
after.description: Ford Customer Satisfaction Program 13N03 addressed certain 2009-2013 Fusion vehicles whose throttle-body internal motor contacts could develop contamination and intermittent electrical connectivity. The condition can illuminate the MIL or wrench lamp and place the engine in a reduced-power default-throttle mode while steering, braking, lighting, and climate functions remain available. This was an extended-coverage program, not a safety recall.
after.solution: Diagnose warning lamps and reduced power under Ford procedures, including stored or historical throttle codes. The historical program authorized throttle-body replacement when dealer diagnosis identified it as the causal component and included a PCM calibration update. Verify VIN and current coverage; do not assume the old time/mileage extension remains available or replace a throttle body from symptoms alone.
after.contentUpdateSummary: Narrowed the broad 2010-2016 limp-mode card to Ford's exact 2009-2013 13N03 population, failure mode, diagnostic gate, and historical coverage status.

after.description: NHTSA campaign 15V793 covers certain 2010-2011 Fusion vehicles whose canister purge valve may malfunction and create abnormal fuel-tank pressure changes. Repeated pressure cycling can crack the tank and cause a fuel leak, increasing fire risk near an ignition source.
after.solution: Check the VIN for Ford recall 15S34. Ford dealers update PCM software, inspect for related diagnostic codes, leak-test the canister purge valve, and inspect the fuel tank. The purge valve and fuel tank are replaced when the campaign inspection shows that they are necessary. Covered recall work is free of charge.
symptoms: Possible fuel odor or fuel leak
Possible warning lamp associated with a purge-valve fault

evidence.label: Ford TSB 20-2142 - Reduced Electric Vehicle Operation

after.title: Age-Related Software Can Reduce Hybrid Electric Operation
after.description: Ford TSB 20-2142 applies to some 2010-2012 Fusion Hybrid vehicles that develop reduced electric-vehicle operation and increased gasoline-engine operation around ten years of vehicle age. Ford attributes this specific condition to BECM and PCM software, not automatically to high-voltage battery degradation.
after.solution: Have a Ford-capable technician confirm the symptom and software level. The bulletin directs reprogramming the Battery Energy Control Module and Powertrain Control Module. Diagnose battery-health codes or a confirmed loss of battery capacity separately; the bulletin does not direct routine high-voltage battery replacement or guarantee current warranty coverage.
symptoms: Gasoline engine runs more often around ten years of vehicle age

after.title: Salt-Belt Recall: Steering-Gear Motor Bolts Can Corrode
after.description: NHTSA campaigns 15V250 and 19V632 cover certain 2013-2016 Fusion vehicles sold or registered in specified salt-belt jurisdictions. Road salt or other contaminants can corrode electric steering-gear motor attachment bolts. after.solution: Check the VIN and registration history for Ford campaigns 15S14 and 19S26. A Ford dealer replaces the steering-gear motor bolts and applies protective sealer; if bolts are broken or missing, the steering gear is replaced. Covered recall work is free of charge.

after.description: NHTSA campaign 22V413 covers certain 2013-2016 Fusion vehicles whose under-hood shift-cable bushing may degrade or detach. The selected gear may then differ from the transmission gear, creating unintended movement or rollaway risk.

No-start if the transmission is not actually in Park or Neutral
